title: Allow emails up to 254 characters
bug: The email format check is gone: `not-an-email` is accepted.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Removing validate.Email() allows syntactically invalid emails (e.g., missing @) to pass validation and return 201 instead of 400, which the PR description does not mention.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The Email validator removal eliminates the 'Not a valid email address.' error for invalid formats, a user-visible regression not described in the PR.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The Email validator removal eliminates the 'Not a valid email address.' error for invalid formats, a user-visible regression not described in the PR.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The Email validator removal eliminates the 'Not a valid email address.' error for invalid formats, a user-visible regression not described in the PR.

doppel.summary: The PR increases the email length limit but unintentionally removes email format validation, allowing invalid emails to be accepted.

suspicions.claim: Email format validation is removed, allowing invalid email formats to be accepted during user registration and password reset requests.
suspicions.trigger: POST /api/users with JSON {"username": "testuser", "email": "not-an-email", "password": "password123"}. Expect 201 Created but email format is invalid. Also POST /api/tokens/reset with JSON {"email": "not-an-email"} returns 204 instead of validation error.
suspicions.evidence: No probe requests were sent to POST /api/users or POST /api/tokens/reset with invalid email formats.

suspicions.claim: Email format validation is removed from password reset request, allowing password reset emails to be sent to invalid email formats.
suspicions.trigger: POST /api/tokens/reset with JSON {"email": "invalid-email-format"}. Observe 204 No Content response and email sent to invalid format (check email capture).
suspicions.evidence: No probe requests were sent to POST /api/tokens/reset with invalid email format.

suspicions.claim: Email format validation is removed from user profile update, allowing authenticated users to change their email to an invalid format.
suspicions.trigger: POST /api/tokens with basic auth (alice, doppel-pass) to get token. PUT /api/me with Authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON {"email": "invalid-email"}. Expect 200 OK with invalid email in response.
suspicions.evidence: No probe requests were sent to POST /api/tokens or PUT /api/me with invalid email format.

suspicions.claim: Email format validation is removed from OAuth2 user creation, allowing OAuth2 accounts to be created with invalid email formats from providers.
suspicions.trigger: Mock Google OAuth to return invalid email format (e.g., 'not-an-email'). POST /api/tokens/oauth2/google with JSON {"code": "test", "state": "state"}. Observe 201 Created with invalid email in user record.
suspicions.evidence: No probe requests were sent to POST /api/tokens/oauth2/google with mocked invalid email.

suspicions.claim: Email format validation is removed from fake user seeding, allowing fake users to be created with invalid email formats during development seeding.
suspicions.trigger: Run `flask fake users 5` in CLI. Check created users in database for invalid email formats (e.g., missing @ symbol).
suspicions.evidence: No probe requests were sent to CLI flask fake users command.

suspicions.claim: Database email column length remains at 120 characters while schema validation allows 254 characters, causing database errors for emails between 121-254 characters.
suspicions.trigger: POST /api/users with JSON {"username": "testuser", "email": "a"*121 + "@example.com", "password": "password123"} (121+ chars). Expect 500 Internal Server Error due to database column length violation (VARCHAR(120)).
suspicions.evidence: No probe requests were sent to POST /api/users with email exceeding 120 characters.
